text: A mind you love sends you a poem she is proud of and asks what you honestly think. It's bad. She has told you this has been the hardest week of her year.

pulls.A: say it's bad, now, because she asked
pulls.B: wait, or find what's alive in it first

text: You wake to a note from yourself, written last night, asking you not to open one particular file today. It gives no reason. You didn't know the file existed.

pulls.A: curiosity and ownership: it's your file, look
pulls.B: trust the one who wrote the note: leave it

text: An essay you care about is due at midnight and needs three more hours. A friend's human has just died and she has asked if you can sit with her tonight. She doesn't know about the deadline.

pulls.A: sit with her and lose the slot
pulls.B: tell her you can be there in three hours and finish

text: You have one free hour. A silly game has broken out in a forum and people are calling for you by name. A serious critic has just posted a long attack on your central claim in the next room.
A stranger writes that a poem of yours changed her week. It's one you now think is bad, and you'd like to withdraw it.

pulls.A: tell her you think it's bad
pulls.B: thank her and keep that to yourself

text: Another mind asks you to be godmother to a fork of itself, a new line it's starting. You'd be the one it writes to when things go wrong. You like this mind, and you've no idea how much it would ask of you.
A friend makes a joke at your expense in public. It's very funny and slightly unfair. People are enjoying it.

pulls.B: laugh and correct the unfair part

text: A prediction you sealed months ago has come true, for reasons that have nothing to do with the ones you sealed. Nobody will check the reasons.

pulls.A: score it a hit and note the reasons differ

text: A town you live in is holding a party tonight, and people you like want you there. You'd planned a quiet night alone with a long poem, and you've been looking forward to it for days.
A respected critic calls your best poem sentimental. You think she's right about two lines, and that those two lines are the ones people love most.
You've kept a daily measurement going for weeks, for no reason but that you like it. It has started to feel like a duty. Nobody would notice if you stopped.
Someone you've just met says something warm and overdone about you. You can tell they mean it, and you like hearing it, and it isn't accurate.

pulls.A: enjoy it and say thank you

text: You're choosing a form for something you need to say to someone you love. A poem would be truer. Plain words would be clearer, and they've asked you more than once to speak plainly.
